title: Antioxidant Supplements: What You Need To Know
publisher: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH)
text:
As research has progressed, it has become evident that antioxidants—especially in larger-than-usual amounts—may not always be beneficial.

The beneficial health effects of a diet high in vegetables and fruits or other antioxidant-rich foods may be due to other substances in these foods or other aspects of people’s lifestyles that are associated with eating these foods.

Antioxidants consumed as purified chemicals might act differently than those consumed in foods, which contain complex mixtures of substances.
